content: {"summary":"Login 503 errors rose gradually in April 2025 because auth-service connections to auth-db-01 began failing after the database presented an expired TLS certificate; the certificate file on disk had been renewed but PostgreSQL had not reloaded it, so new connections were rejected while older ones aged out.","likely_cause":"PostgreSQL on auth-db-01 continued using the expired server certificate because it was not reloaded after the renewal.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Login error rate increased over minutes as older connections expired and new ones failed.","evidence_ids":["RB-024#4"],"quote":"error-rate alert paged at 09:38."},{"text":"auth-service logs show TLS errors and logins failing with 503 due to expired certificate.","evidence_ids":["RB-024#0"],"quote":"auth-service logs connection errors containing `tls error` and `x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid`, and logins fail with `503`."},{"text":"The server was still presenting the old expired certificate despite a renewed file on disk.","evidence_ids":["RB-024#2"],"quote":"Different serials mean the server is still on the old certificate."},{"text":"Reloading PostgreSQL configuration fixed the TLS errors and restored normal logins.","evidence_ids":["RB-024#4"],"quote":"`pg_reload_conf()` at 09:51 fixed it, and logins were normal again by 09:53."}],"next_checks":["Confirm that pg-cert-renew.timer triggers a PostgreSQL reload after writing new cert files","Verify the certificate serial presented by auth-db-01 matches the on‑disk renewed certificate","Check that the replica auth-db-02 was also reloaded after its cert renewal","Monitor auth-service TLS error metrics for any recurrence"]}
